title: Number parsing & coercion
description: Every input is a string until you parse it — pick the right tool (parseInt, parseFloat, Number, unary `+`) and know why `Number.isNaN` is safer than the global `isNaN`.

reference.code:
// parseInt — leading digits, stops at first non-digit
parseInt('42px', 10);     // 42
parseInt('  -7 ', 10);    // -7
parseInt('0.9', 10);      // 0   (stops at '.')
parseInt('abc', 10);      // NaN

// ALWAYS pass the radix — '0x10' would parse as hex without it
parseInt('0x10', 10);     // 0
parseInt('0x10');         // 16  (legacy hex detection)

// parseFloat — accepts decimals + exponent
parseFloat('3.14abc');    // 3.14
parseFloat('1e3');        // 1000

// Number — STRICT, whole string must be numeric (trims whitespace)
Number('42');             // 42
Number('42px');           // NaN  (unlike parseInt)
Number('');               // 0    (gotcha)
Number('  3.14  ');       // 3.14

// Unary + — same as Number(x), shorter
+'5';                     // 5
+'';                      // 0
+'5px';                   // NaN

// Validation helpers (DO NOT coerce — false for non-numbers)
Number.isInteger(3);       // true
Number.isInteger(3.0);     // true   (3.0 === 3)
Number.isInteger('3');     // false  (no coercion)
Number.isFinite(Infinity); // false
Number.isFinite('1');      // false  (no coercion)
Number.isNaN(NaN);         // true
Number.isNaN('foo');       // false  (no coercion)
isNaN('foo');              // true   (global — coerces first, surprise)
notes: Always pass the radix to `parseInt(s, 10)` — otherwise `'08'` and `'0x10'` get parsed oddly across engines.
`Number('')` and `Number('  ')` are `0`, not `NaN`. Reject empty input explicitly.
Prefer `Number.isNaN(x)` over global `isNaN(x)` — the global coerces first so `isNaN('foo')` is misleadingly `true`.

questions.explain: `parseInt` reads leading digits and stops at the first non-digit.
`Number` is strict — the whole string must be numeric (whitespace-trimmed).
Empty/whitespace-only strings coerce to 0. Validate first.

options: Number.isNaN does not coerce; global isNaN does
Global `isNaN` returns `false` for actual NaN values (the historical bug)

exercises.prompt: Parse the leading integer from the CSS-like string.
Coerce the input only if it is a pure number; otherwise log 'bad'.

L3.prompt: Write `toIntStrict(s)` that returns the integer if `s` is a clean base-10 integer string (optional leading `-`), else `null`. Log results for `'42'`, `'-7'`, `'3.14'`, `' 5 '`, `'5px'`.
hints: Validate with a regex (`/^-?\d+$/`) before coercing.
`Number(s)` is fine once you have confirmed the shape.
